note: Window agent p1990-p1999, 2 Nov 2026. Fixes: Chukotka east of 180 left ownerless at the RSFSR end; the four bantustans left ownerless in April 1994; Belize drawn as a British colony after independence; Podlachia and Sakhalin/Kuril cells drawn as Soviet/Japanese; RUF drawn inside Liberia.

region.text: the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, including the part east of the 180th meridian

events.note: Dec 1991: the Federation's founding region leaves Chukotka east of 180 degrees (about 400 cells) without an owner when the RSFSR ends; they are the Federation's. The page: 'Chukotka, officially the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, is the easternmost federal subject of Russia' and 'In 1991, Chukotka declared its separation to become a subject of the Russian Federation in its own right.'

region.text: the Transkei, Venda and Ciskei homelands (201 cells), which the vassal_end events of April 1994 leave ownerless

events.note: 27 April 1994: 'all Bantustans (both nominally independent and self-governing) were dismantled' and 'their territories reincorporated into the Republic of South Africa with effect from 27 April 1994'. The vassal_end events release Transkei, Venda and Ciskei to nobody; this puts them back under South Africa. Bophuthatswana does not resolve in the gazetteer and is already South African land in the draft.

region.text: Belize as independent: 'It has an area of 22,970 square kilometres'

events.note: 'Belize achieved its independence from the United Kingdom on 21 September 1981.' The start anchor of 1990 still gives 75 interior cells to the British Colonial Empire (drawn as a UK colony until its 1996 keyframe drops them to nobody); they are Belize's.

correction.text: the strip on the Sierra Leone side of the Sierra Leone-Liberian border to which the SLA 'pushed the RUF' in March 1993 (Liberian land not included)

keyframe_overrides.why: The page says the SLA 'pushed the RUF to the Sierra Leone - Liberia border' and describes no RUF-held land in Liberia; the three-cell border band took 44 Liberian cells from Liberia.

union.text: the strip on the Sierra Leone side of the border (Liberian land not included)

correction.text: the rebel-held areas of Sierra Leone: the Eastern Province and the border strip on the Sierra Leone side; no Liberian land

keyframe_overrides.why: Same cut as the 1993 keyframe: the RUF fought in Sierra Leone from bases in Liberia, and the page maps no RUF-held Liberian land. The keyframe runs 1994-2001, so the cut also acts in 2000-2001.

correction.text: the Russian Federation as it stood when the Soviet Union dissolved: the 1992 Cliopatria shape used one year early; plus Chukotka east of 180 degrees, which the Cliopatria outline (bbox ends at longitude 180.0) leaves out

keyframe_overrides.why: Cliopatria's Russian Federation shapes stop at the 180th meridian, so about 400 cells of the easternmost federal subject ('Chukotka, officially the Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, is the easternmost federal subject of Russia'; it 'declared its separation to become a subject of the Russian Federation in its own right' in 1991) are dropped at every keyframe snap. The base shape is the dossier's own correction, unchanged.

rulings.why: Bialystok was 'incorporated into the Byelorussian SSR from 1939 to 1941' and 'transferred back to Poland' on 20 September 1944; it was the capital of the Bialystok Voivodeship of the People's Republic of Poland, so Podlachia and the Lublin border cells were Polish, not Byelorussian, in 1990-1991.

South Sakhalin, Tyuleniy Island and the southern Kuril cells were Soviet-held; the page: 'The disputed islands are under Russian administration as the South Kuril District' and 'The Japanese inhabitants of the Kurils were expelled'. Japan only claims the islands.
